presentation.purpose: Choose which source values matter at each requested position.

learning.title: Explore Multihead attention in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Choose which source values matter at each requested position.
learning.disclosureTitle: How sequence comparisons and blocked connections work
learning.formula: Choose which source values matter at each requested position.
paragraphs: A sequence is an ordered list of positions, such as readings over time. Each position contains several values. A batch is a group of independent observations; this block keeps observations first.

A query describes what a requested position is looking for. A key describes a source position so it can be compared with the query. A value is the source information mixed into the result. A head makes one separate set of comparisons.

Model width sets the query and result width. It must divide evenly between Heads. Key width and Value width can use that same width or an explicit different width. Use bias are small learned additions. Added learned or empty source positions extend the source used for mixing.

Output attention weights exposes the actual share assigned to each source position. Average across heads averages those shares across groups; turning it off keeps a separate table for every group. Connection weights are results to inspect, not another bank of learned settings.

A mask is a table of blocked connections. One means blocked and zero means allowed throughout this canvas. Use mask connection enables the matching input. Earlier positions only is a square causal arrangement: each position can use itself and earlier positions. Every query must retain an eligible original source after combined connection and position masks.

No context is secretly stored between calls, and there is no automatic key/value cache. Floating inputs and outputs use dense float32 on CPU or MPS; supplied masks use exact int64 binary arrays. Sequence and observation counts, named outputs and allocation budgets are checked.

Drop probability temporarily hides comparison weights during training and is zero during evaluation. CPU supports exact checkpoint continuation; MPS supports explicit weights-only restarting. Input influence means how a small source change affects the result. Guided, practice and private checks use changed examples to measure this understanding.

Configuration uses stacked controls with Apply and Revert. Weights and biases selects a named layer and parameter where applicable; starting values affect fresh training, while an exactly compatible checkpoint restores saved values. Disconnect connected or exposed mask/weight ports before removing them. Detailed meanings and the original lesson link remain in Information.

presentation.purpose: Create explicit blocked connections and source positions from sequence references.

learning.title: Explore Attention mask in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Create explicit blocked connections and source positions from sequence references.
learning.disclosureTitle: How sequence comparisons and blocked connections work
learning.formula: Create explicit blocked connections and source positions from sequence references.
paragraphs: A sequence is an ordered list of positions, such as readings over time. Each position contains several values. A batch is a group of independent observations; this block keeps observations first.

A query describes what a requested position is looking for. A key describes a source position so it can be compared with the query. A value is the source information mixed into the result. A head makes one separate set of comparisons.

Connect floating query and key references so the block can derive position counts and observation count. It creates mask and padding outputs using whole-number binary values: one blocks a connection or source position, zero allows it. No floating values are reinterpreted as mask coordinates.

In Blocked pairs mode, corresponding entries in Blocked query positions and Blocked key positions describe one blocked pair. Positions start at zero; pairs must be unique and both lists must have equal length. Padding positions blocks those columns in the mask output and also creates the padding output. This makes the same source blocks usable by attention that has only one mask connection. These same configured choices apply to every observation; arbitrary per-observation mask data is outside this utility.

Earlier positions only requires equal query and source lengths. Nonempty paired lists require Blocked pairs mode. The downstream attention block refuses a fully blocked combined row rather than producing an unusable result.
This utility owns no learned settings or gradients. It creates bounded int64 masks on the references' device. It is taught inside the attention lessons and earns no extra framework coverage.

Configuration uses Blocked query/key pair rows and Padding positions. Add or remove rows explicitly, then Apply; Revert discards the draft. In the assessed lab, corresponding query/key position lists describe the same pairs. Each position starts at zero. Information explains the two real mask outputs.

presentation.purpose: Rotate Query and Key feature pairs by their sequence positions; position settings stay inline and Value bypasses this transform.

learning.title: Rotary position · RoPE
learning.subtitle: Position changes Query and Key, not Value
learning.formula: θ(j,p) = p × base^(−2j/R) / scale; (a,b) → (a cos θ − b sin θ, a sin θ + b cos θ)
paragraphs: Query and Key carry floating tensors through Rotary position into attention. Value connects directly to attention. Starting position and position scale are inline settings, never configuration edges.

For [B,H,T,D], choose sequence axis2 (or −2). Features are always last. At position0 the rotation is the identity. Each coordinate pair keeps its squared magnitude, while relative Query/Key angle changes comparisons. RoPE does not mask future positions; the attention mask remains a separate attention setting.

Adjacent pairs use (0,1),(2,3)… and match the Llama convention. Split halves uses (0,R/2),(1,R/2+1)… . The custom rotated prefix must be even and fit the feature width; the suffix is unchanged. Switching a convention is an architecture change, not checkpoint conversion.

Open the editable causal token model and run Train, then Generate. Inspect Query and Key outputs in Results, including other heads and positions. Compare pairing/base/offset controls and reject an odd rotated width. This practice is unscored and the tiny synthetic model is not a full Llama or a language-quality benchmark.

Positions restart at the configured offset for each complete forward. The current generator recomputes its suffix context without a KV cache; training, generation and exported code use this same convention. Position scale is a linear divisor, not NTK/YaRN scaling. RoPE owns no learned weights or persistent cache.
